Subject: Draft

Spent the last two Saturdays redoing the electric in a buddy’s shed. I’m 49 years old, been doing this 26 years, and apparently I can still open a panel and find a whole new reason to stand there with my hands on my hips.

Inside the panel door, in Sharpie:

SHED - DONT TOUCH - RON

Buddy’s wife is standing there. First thing out of her mouth is “who’s Ron”

Like I know. Lady I just got here. Apparently Ron’s the only one allowed to touch it, and after looking inside I’d say Ron should’ve included himself in that rule.

Here’s what we had.

Three orange extension cords plugged into each other, out the basement window, across the yard and under the deck. That wasn’t temporary power. That was permanent optimism.

A splice wrapped in duct tape. Not electrical tape. DUCT tape. Somebody looked at that and said yep, same stuff holding the dryer vent together, oughta handle electricity.

A 30 amp breaker feeding 14 gauge wire. That one’s not funny. The breaker is supposed to protect the wire. Putting a bigger breaker on undersized wire doesn’t give you more power. It lets that wire get hotter than it should before the breaker does its job.

An outlet wired with speaker wire. Great if you want to hear the fire coming, I guess.

A regular outlet with a GFCI sticker stuck on it. I stared at that one awhile. Might put a sticker on my truck that says “paid off” and see if the bank goes along with it.

Ceiling fan box held up with ONE drywall screw. One. Working harder than anybody else on the property.

Mouse nest in the junction box. Mice were fine. Completely unbothered. Only residents who hadn’t complained about the electrical.

Now I don’t think whoever did this was evil. Cheap and a little proud, probably. That’s most of these jobs. Somebody gets something to turn on and figures that means they did it right.

Working and safe are two different things.

This stuff burns houses down. A bad connection can heat up where you can’t see it. Wrong wire, wrong breaker, no real ground-fault protection. None of that gets fixed because the light comes on when you hit the switch.

It’s redone now. Buried feed, proper breaker and GFCI protection, proper boxes and outlets, fan supported by a brace instead of a prayer. The mice will have to make other arrangements.

Please call a licensed electrician. Not your buddy with a YouTube video and a bucket of leftover wire. Ask questions. Get it checked. I’d rather explain what’s wrong with it than hear afterward that somebody got hurt.

And if you’re labeling a panel, tell me what the breaker feeds. I don’t need a threatening note from Ron.
